title: post-incident-slo-capacity-mapping-template-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document is a practical template and decision guide for post-incident reviews that explicitly maps SLOs, error budget consumption, and capacity signals to incident severity, remediation priorities, and follow-up actions. It is intended for SREs, oncall engineers, and service owners who run post-incident reviews (PIRs). Use this template to standardize evidence collection, causal analysis, and capacity-driven remediation work accepted into the reliability backlog.

Scope and audience:
- Covers incidents that impact core Redwood inference services (runtime, routing, KV cache, autoscaler, ingress) and adjacent control plane components that affect customer-facing SLOs.
- Not intended for purely business-side issues (billing portal outages) unless they cause measurable user-facing SLO regressions.
- Primary audience: SRE oncall, service owners, platform reliability leads, and incident reviewers.

Why this exists:
- We observed inconsistent mapping from error-budget consumption to concrete post-incident work. That led to either under-emphasis of high-impact capacity issues or over-commitment of development resources for low-impact degradations. This template enforces a reproducible mapping: evidence -> SLO impact -> capacity signal -> prioritized remediation.

Quick reference: 
- Severity mapping (high-level):
  1) Sev1: >5% global user-visible error-rate increase sustained >5m OR >=25% of customers experiencing P50 latency >2x baseline OR catastrophic capacity collapse (node pool down)
  2) Sev2: measurable SLO breach window or cumulative error-budget burn >2% in 1 hour for a tier-1 model/service
  3) Sev3: transient spikes, config rollbacks, or non-customer-facing degradations with localized impact

- Post-incident timeboxes: PIR within 72 hours, follow-up plan within 14 days, remediation backlog item or cancel decision within 30 days.

Incident metadata (fill at start of PIR):
- Incident ID: (e.g., INC-2026-0718-23)
- Primary service(s): (e.g., serving-runtime-gpu, request-router)
- Initial severity: (Sev1/Sev2/Sev3)
- Start time / End time / Duration
- Oncall rotation and primary responder
- Summary (1–2 sentences)

Evidence checklist (required attachments):
- Telemetry: SLO dashboards, error-rate timeseries, latency P50/P95/P99 for affected tenants (CSV or screenshot)
- Capacity signals: node-usage, GPU memory pressure, queue length, scheduler wait times, eviction counts
- Autoscaler logs: scale decisions, timestamped metrics for scaling triggers
- Deployment events: rollouts, image hashes, config changes, feature-flag changes
- Traces: representative distributed traces for failed requests (trace IDs)
- Service logs: filtered logs around incident window (include sampling keys / tenant IDs)
- Postmortem evidence archive link: (Confluence / GCS / internal artifact storage)

SLO / Error budget mapping table (copy into the PIR):
| SLO name | Target | Observed window | Deviation | Error budget consumed | Tenant impact (est) | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| inference-generation-availability | 99.95% (30d) | 99.40% (1h) | -0.55% | 40% of hourly budget | 18% of active tenants had 5+ failures | autoscaler delayed recovery under load |
| embedding-p99-latency | <120ms | 310ms (5m) | +190ms | N/A (latency SLO) | All tenants below baseline SL tier | quantized-serving tails increased |

Decision criteria (how severity & follow-up are derived):
1) If error-budget lost in rolling 1h >= 20% for a tier-1 SLO -> escalate to Sev1 review and schedule emergency remediation planning.
2) If capacity signals show sustained GPU memory pressure >85% for >10m correlated with SLO degradation -> prioritize capacity engineering (slot increase, scheduler tuning, or model-pin rollback).
3) If incident caused by deployment config -> owner must provide rollback, canary gating improvements, and at least one automation test in CI.
4) If multiple tenants impacted but error-budget loss <5% -> classify as Sev2 and prioritize mitigations that prevent recurrence (alert tuning, circuit-breakers).

RCA template (structured, short answers):
- Problem statement (one sentence):
- Impacted SLO(s) and customer-visible effect: 
- Root cause hypothesis (what failed at the system boundary):
- Evidence supporting hypothesis (list items with links):
- Contributing factors (ranked): 1) , 2) , 3)
- Why automation/manual steps failed (if applicable):
- Immediate mitigations taken and timestamps:
- Long-term remediation proposals (3 options with cost/effort and owner):

Capacity signal catalog (mapping common signals to actions):
- GPU memory pressure >85% (sustained 10m):
  - Likely causes: model state growth, KV cache leak, incorrect batch sizing, hot-tenant pressure
  - Immediate action: trigger tenant throttling for heavy tenants, enable graceful degradation for non-critical models, add emergency nodes (if pool has spare capacity)
  - Follow-up: model-level quota, autoscaler tuning, KV cache TTL snapshotting
- Scheduler queue length >1000 requests / 30s:
  - Likely causes: ingress spike, downstream dependency slow, autoscaler cold start delay
  - Immediate action: enable backpressure / shed best-effort routes, route traffic to fallback region/model, signal autoscaler with pre-warm policy
  - Follow-up: implement request-level pre-warming and ramping policy in the autoscaler config
- Node eviction count >0.5%/hr:
  - Likely causes: OOM, driver crash, ephemeral storage saturation
  - Immediate action: remove faulty AMIs, drain pool, alert kernel/drivers team
  - Follow-up: kernel upgrade plan and crash-dump automation

Incident-to-backlog decision matrix (use during PIR closure):
- Tier A remediation (must do within 14d): 1) Direct root cause fix that prevents recurrence of Sev1-like capacity collapse; 2) Fix when error-budget consumption >25% and >1% customers impacted.
- Tier B remediation (plan within 30d, implement within 90d): performance tuning, alerting gaps, runbook updates.
- Tier C remediation (deferred): non-critical documentation, minor telemetry increases.

Concrete runbook changes to consider (check at PIR):
- Add capacity signals to the oncall dashboard: GPU memory heatmap, per-tenant qps, scheduler backlog by model-size.
- Create an automated playbook for emergency node pool add/remove that an oncall can trigger from the Slack/CICD bot with RBAC controls.
- Add synthetic canaries that exercise long-tail quantized paths and gating thresholds before each major rollout.

Execution checklist for PIR facilitator (numbered procedure):
1) Validate required evidence is attached. If telemetry is missing, escalate to telemetry owner and kick off a 48h evidence collection window.
2) Present SLO mapping table and a one-slide timeline of events.
3) Confirm root cause hypothesis and mark "hypothesis confidence" (low/medium/high).
4) Decide remediation tier and owner. For Tier A assign a primary and secondary engineer with expected deliverable and deadline.
5) Add remediation to reliability backlog board and tag with incident ID and SLO impacted.
6) Re-run post-incident synthetic checks and confirm recovery for affected tenants.
7) Publish PIR summary to stakeholders and archive evidence.

Follow-up triggers and automation hooks (examples):
- If same SLO is implicated in 3 incidents within 90 days -> create a reliability initiative ticket and require dedicated capacity experiments.
- If autoscaler back-pressure is activated twice in a week for same model -> require pre-warming policy change and owner-level retrospective.
- Automation: a nightly job will re-evaluate incident SLO tables and flag stale remediations older than 30d to the reliability lead.

Example CLI and query snippets (for evidence collection):
- Query recent errors for a tenant: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://telemetry.internal/api/errors?tenant_id=TENANT123&from=2026-10-01T10:00Z&to=2026-10-01T12:00Z"
- PromQL: avg_over_time(request_latency_ms_p95{service="inference"}[10m]) > 200
- K8s: kubectl top pods --namespace serving | sort -rk 3 | head -n 20

Ownership and escalation contacts (examples):
- SRE oncall rotation: #sre-oncall in Slack (primary contact during incident)
- Serving runtime lead: Marco Ruiz (marco@redwood.ai)
- Autoscaler owner: Elena Kim (elena@redwood.ai)
- Telemetry owner: Derrick Wang (derrick@redwood.ai)

Retention & evidence storage policy:
- Store all incident artifacts in GCS under gs://redwood-incidents/YYYY/MM/INC-ID/ with an index.json listing attachments.
- Evidence retention: 540 days for Sev1/Sev2, 180 days for Sev3.

Appendix: sample outcome summary (to publish)
- Short summary: (1–2 sentences) state impact and fix.
- Timeline highlights: bullet list with timestamps and actions.
- Root cause and contributing factors: 2–3 bullets.
- Remediation plan and owners: list with due dates.
- Business impact estimate: lost requests, customer support tickets, revenue exposure (if known).

References and related reading:
- SLO escalation and capacity triggers (link internal)
- Autoscaler design spec (link internal)
- Incident evidence standards (link internal)

Notes and versioning:
- This template v1.0 created 2026-07-06 by Aisha Patel. Last updated 2026-10-02 to clarify capacity triggers and retention policy.
- Changes: added nightly job automation trigger and expanded capacity signal catalog.

End of document.
